unit.name: Ecological Adaptations, Succession and Ecological Services (Botany)

chapter: Ecological Adaptations, Succession and Ecological Services
question_text: Write a brief account on the classification of xerophytes.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 13, book p.36, SAQ 1. The book's three groups and all six examples are kept (Tribulus; Asparagus, Opuntia, Aloe; Nerium, Casuarina); the definition of a xerophyte, which the book omits, is added because the question says 'classification of xerophytes' and a classification needs the thing being classified named first. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The 1+1+1+1 split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Ecological Adaptations, Succession and Ecological Services · 4 marks

steps.label: Definition and the three groups
lines: Xerophytes are plants that grow in dry
They are classified into three groups:
steps.why: A classification answer is marked on its headings first. Naming all three groups in the opening lines secures the structure mark before any detail is written.
common_mistakes: Starting straight with ephemerals and never naming the three groups together.
Writing four or five groups. The standard classification has exactly three.
steps.memory_tip: Three groups by what happens in the drought: the life cycle finishes early, water is stored, or the plant withstands it.
steps.margin_note: Open with the three names in a numbered line. That line alone is one mark.

steps.label: Ephemerals
lines: the whole life cycle in a very short
period, within a few weeks of the rain,
and pass the dry season as seeds.
steps.why: An ephemeral is not present as a growing plant during the drought. It germinates, flowers and sets seed while water is present, so the short life cycle IS the adaptation.
common_mistakes: Calling them perennials. Ephemerals are annuals with a very short life.
Leaving out the example. Each group carries its own example mark.
steps.memory_tip: Ephemeral means short-lived. The whole life cycle is over before the soil dries.
steps.margin_note: Two lines and one example per group. Do not expand any one group.

steps.label: Succulents
lines: Succulents: they absorb large amounts of
water in the rainy season and store it as
steps.why: Succulents are named by WHICH organ stores the water, so the three sub-types with one example each are what the examiner is counting in this mark.
common_mistakes: Giving one example only. The three sub-types each need their own plant.
Swapping Opuntia and Aloe. Opuntia stores in the stem, Aloe in the leaf.
steps.memory_tip: Root, stem, leaf — Asparagus, Opuntia, Aloe, in that order.
steps.margin_note: Write the three sub-types as a lettered list; it reads as three points.

steps.label: Non-succulents
lines: They are perennials that withstand long
periods of drought without storing water,
using deep roots, thick cuticle, sunken
steps.why: Non-succulents endure the drought while still growing, so they carry the morphological and anatomical adaptations: sunken stomata, thick cuticle, reduced leaves and deep roots.
common_mistakes: Writing that non-succulents store water. Storing water is what makes a plant a succulent.
Calling them annuals. They are perennials.
steps.memory_tip: Non-succulent = no stored water, so every other feature reduces water loss.
steps.margin_note: End with this group and its example; it is the one the examiner reads last.

insider_note: Four marks means four blocks. Name all three groups in the first line, then give exactly one short paragraph and one example each, and the answer fits the time.
